newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary farmers cancel talks, say will close roads.
newsitem.headline: Hungary farmers cancel talks, say will close roads.

text.p: Hungarian farmers cancelled talks with the government on Friday and said they would go ahead with demonstrations meant to close down many of the country's roads next week.

"Unfortunately, the government aims to avoid dealing with important questions and only wants to stop our demonstration," organisers Gyula Kosa and Gyozo Zsikla said in a fax sent to the finance ministry and made available to Reuters.
"The organising committee decided to cancel the talks... We will hold the demonstrations as planned," it added.

Earlier this week, the farmers said that if the government did not meet their demands for changing 1997 tax regulations, they would set up over 25 road blocks outside key towns for 72 hours beginning Monday morning.

The farmers presented a petition last week to the agricultural ministry demanding that the cabinet should withdraw tax and social security measures introduced on January 1, which they say jeopardise their livelihood.
Finance Minister Peter Medgyessy told a news conference Friday afternoon that the government remained open to talks with the farmers.
Fulop Benedek, state secretary for agriculture, said the government would respond positively to several demands, including administrative simplifications, and the abolition of a minimal contribution.

Medgyessy, however, said that the government would not exempt full-time farmers from social security contributions and would not allow farmers to get tax exemptions without itemising income and expenditures.
He added that the farmers' leaders seemed to be more interested in showing their general displeasure with the government than with resolving the dispute.
Kosa last week described the socialist-Liberal government as "a Jewish-communist gang" which wanted to destroy Hungarian agriculture.
Hungarian opposition parties said they supported the farmers but distanced themselves from Kosa's anti-Semitism.
